sentences.text: Incomplete fossils reveal dromaeosaurid characteristics in the vertebrae and arm bones, closely resembling the famous Deinonychus.

While the adult animal was slightly smaller than Deinonychus, reaching about 2 meters in length, a 2019 volumetric analysis estimated the specimen to be 1.65 meters long, 54 centimeters high at the hip, and 12.8 kilograms in body mass.

A referred right humerus has a well-developed deltopectoral crest, suggesting the forearm was used for raptorial functions.
Amateur paleontologists Patrick Méchin and Annie Méchin-Salessy discovered the remains of a small theropod in the Grès à Reptiles Formation between 1992 and 1995.
Jean Le Loeuff and Eric Buffetaut named the species Variraptor mechinorum in 1998.
The genus name Variraptor combines Latin Varus, referring to the Var River in southern France, and the word raptor meaning thief.
Le Loeuff and Buffetaut described Variraptor as a maniraptoran theropod and member of the family Dromaeosauridae, a classification generally accepted.
Variraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 77 to 69 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
In 2000, Oliver Rauhut expressed doubts about the dromaeosaurid classification, assigning it instead to the broader group Coelurosauria.
In 2009, Buffetaut and Phomphen Chanthasit defended the validity of Variraptor, arguing the holotype possessed a unique combination of traits.
A 2022 phylogenetic analysis recovered Variraptor within Unenlagiinae.
In 2023, assuming Variraptor and Pyroraptor are valid species, both were recovered as dromaeosaurs, though their phylogenetic affinities were not well established.
